answer.text:
The Initial Source logic for renewal opportunities was changed so that:

- The Initial Source for renewals will always reference the oldest Closed-Won, New Business opportunity on the account, not the linked source opportunity.
- If there is no Closed-Won, New Business opportunity on the account, the Initial Source for renewals will default to "Unknown".

This decision was made by Ken Watanabe in the Channel Ops sync meeting on June 3, 2026. The change was implemented in MR 20005 on June 8, 2026. The meeting record gives no further reason.

Relevant quotes from the meeting:
- "The Initial Source for renewals will always reference the oldest Closed-Won, New Biz opp on the account, not the linked source opp."
- "I’d say we default to Unknown if there’s no Closed-Won, New Biz opp."

nodes.label: Subscription/Renewal Management Process
nodes.text:
As of FY23, the Order Management team proactively reviews and corrects bad renewal data.

#### Background

It is important to have clean, correct renewal data - both for forecasting purposes, ATR (Available to Renew, aka ARR Basis) analysis, and general data cleanliness.

Our goal is to maintain 1:1 ratio of Renewal Opportunity to Customer Subscription:

- Every Customer Subscription should link to one open or closed Renewal Opportunity
  - This would not be the case for: Legacy/bad data, automation failures, manual renewal opportunity creation, etc.
